entries.title: Jeremiah 7:1
segments:
vv 1-15. 
 
As the Israelites in Samuel's time thought that the presence of God's ark would give them victory over the Philistines, though they repented not of their transgressions against him; so the Jews in Jeremiah's day who burned incense to idols, and their descendants who crucified the Saviour and persecuted his apostles, believed that God's temple, with its divinely appointed services, would make them secure from danger. All who now put their trust for salvation in outward ordinances and privileges, without inward repentance and obedience, are guilty of the same folly, and must come to the same ruin.

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:4
segments: The temple of the Lord are these; these buildings; the temple properly so called, with its several courts.  They said, These are "the temple of the Lord," and therefore he will defend them and all who worship in them from injury.  Thus the Jews put their trust in outward privileges, and not in holiness of heart and life.

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:10
segments: We are delivered to do all these abominations; more exactly, "We are delivered; in order to do all these abominations."  The words, "We are delivered," are those of the people expressing their confidence that their relation to God and his temple makes them safe from all fear of evil.  The words that follow, "in order to do all these abominations," are those of the prophet, showing the fruit of this false confidence.

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:11
segments: A den of robbers; a den to protect robbers, since they trusted to it for protection in their robberies.  Compare

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:12
segments: Shiloh; north of Jerusalem, in the tribe of Ephraim.  From Joshua to Samuel it was honored as the abode of the tabernacle and ark.

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:15
segments: Ephraim; that is, the kingdom of Israel, of which Ephraim was the chief tribe.

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:16
segments: There is a limit in sin, beyond which God will no longer hear intercessory prayer or delay his judgments.

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:18
segments:
The queen of heaven; the moon, worshipped as a female deity. 
 
When the members of a family or community sin together, they must also suffer together.

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:19
segments: Me--themselves; does the damage fall on me, or on themselves?

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:21
segments:
Put your burnt-offerings unto your sacrifices; by the Mosaic law the burnt-offerings were to be wholly consumed on the altar; but of the peace-offerings a portion only was burned, and upon the remainder the offerer feasted with his friends.  They are here told to eat their burnt-offerings, if they will, with their peace-offerings, for Jehovah will not accept them. 
 
vv 21-23. 
 
God values outward services only as they are expressions of inward love and obedience, and he will not allow the former to be substituted for the latter.

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:22
segments: I spake not--concerning burnt-offerings; I made not these, but love and obedience your main duty.  Compare

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:24
segments:
vv 24-34. 
 
When men refuse to receive the correction of God's word, he will make them feel the power of his anger.  The awful desolation of ancient Jerusalem is a solemn warning to all cities and nations of what awaits them if they imitate her crimes.

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:29
segments: Cut off thy hair; as a sign of deep grief.
